action: Luke splits wood at the sawhorse, pausing to watch Nate stack another cord with careful precision, measuring the quiet deliberation in his son's hands.
thought: Where did he learn such patience with work?

action: Rebecca stirs a pot of stew at the cabin stove while Jacob sets plates on the table, the smell of hot food carrying out across the yard.
thought: Fed and warm before the next push.

action: Nate carries another armload of split wood to the growing stack, setting each piece with deliberate care, unhurried despite the endless summer light above.
thought: This has to be done right the first time.

action: Tommy runs between the woodpile and sawhorse carrying armloads of smaller pieces, already coated in sawdust and whooping with the joy of real work.
thought: This is it. This is the real thing.

action: Jacob sets the last fork on the table, then spots his brothers through the window and presses his nose against the glass, aching to join the work outside.
thought: How long until I'm old enough to split?

description: Midday on Day 1: Luke pauses at the sawhorse, watching Nate stack split wood with quiet deliberation while Tommy runs between them with armloads, Rebecca calls lunch from the cabin, and Jacob bounces in the doorway.

dialogue.speaker: luke
dialogue.line: Nate, that stack's going to last us good into September.

dialogue.speaker: nate
dialogue.line: We've got time. Might as well do it right.

dialogue.speaker: tommy
dialogue.line: I can move twice as fast as Nate, watch!

dialogue.speaker: nate
dialogue.line: You'll burn out by three o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: luke
dialogue.line: He's not wrong, bud. This is a marathon, not a sprint.

dialogue.speaker: tommy
dialogue.line: I don't get tired, I get better.

dialogue.speaker: rebecca
dialogue.line: Jacob, come help me carry the stew pot outside—we're eating in the sun.

dialogue.speaker: jacob
dialogue.line: Can we eat fast? I want to help with the wood!

dialogue.speaker: rebecca
dialogue.line: We'll eat, then you can hand Nate the small pieces, okay?

dialogue.speaker: jacob
dialogue.line: The SMALL ones? I thought I was ready for big ones!

dialogue.speaker: rebecca
dialogue.line: You're the perfect size for small pieces. That's important work.

dialogue.speaker: luke
dialogue.line: Lunch first, boys. Empty belly makes for sloppy work.

dialogue.speaker: nate
dialogue.line: How much wood do you think we need for the whole winter?

dialogue.speaker: luke
dialogue.line: Five cords minimum. We're on cord one-point-five.

dialogue.speaker: nate
dialogue.line: We can do this.

dialogue.speaker: luke
dialogue.line: I know you can.

dialogue.speaker: tommy
dialogue.line: I'll split half a cord myself by dinner!

dialogue.speaker: rebecca
dialogue.line: Tommy, you'll split exactly what your dad tells you to split.

dialogue.speaker: tommy
dialogue.line: That's no fun.

dialogue.speaker: luke
dialogue.line: Fun's everyone making it healthy to winter.

dialogue.speaker: jacob
dialogue.line: Will we get snow way up here?

dialogue.speaker: rebecca
dialogue.line: So much snow. Now come on, let's eat while it's hot.
